1.title: The Processes: Controlling, Delivery, Stage Boundaries and Closing
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: The Processes: Controlling, Delivery, Stage Boundaries and Closing. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Controlling a stage. Managing product delivery. Managing a stage boundary. Closing a project. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (fifteen percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: Controlling a stage
1.text: Controlling a stage. Purpose: assign work, monitor it, deal with issues, report progress to the board, and take corrective action so the stage stays within tolerance. Objectives include: work is authorized and agreed, progress is monitored, issues and risks are managed, and the board is kept informed. Context: it is the project manager's day-to-day process in each delivery stage. It uses work packages, checkpoint reports and highlight reports.

1.title: Managing product delivery
1.text: Managing product delivery. Purpose: control the link between the project manager and the team manager(s) by placing formal requirements on accepting, executing and delivering project work. Objectives include: work is agreed (a work package accepted), delivered to the agreed quality, and progress reported back. Context: it is the team manager's process; it receives work packages from the project manager and returns completed products.

1.title: Managing a stage boundary
1.text: Managing a stage boundary. Purpose: enable the board to review the success of the current stage, approve the next stage plan, review the updated project plan and confirm continued business justification and acceptable risk. Objectives include: the board has enough information, the business case and plans are updated, and lessons are captured. Context: it occurs near the end of every stage except the last. Main outputs: the end stage report and the next stage plan (or an exception plan). Exam tip: Stage boundary equals review this stage, plan the next, confirm the business case. No stage boundary at the end of the last stage: that is closing a project.

1.title: Closing a project
1.text: Closing a project. Purpose: provide a fixed point at which acceptance of the project product is confirmed, and recognize that the objectives in the P I D have been achieved (or the project has nothing more to contribute). Objectives include: verify the product is accepted, hand over to operations, review performance (end project report), record lessons, and plan follow-on actions (including benefits review). Context: it is the final stage of the project, and can also be done early if the board decides to stop the project (a premature close). Exam tip: If the board stops a project early, the project is closed prematurely using the closing a project process.

1.title: Closing a project, continued
1.text: Closing a project. The figure shows this: Controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing a stage boundary and closing a project. Exam tip: Controlling a stage is the project manager's process; managing product delivery is the team manager's. Stage boundary is not used at the end of the last stage.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which process assigns work to be done and monitors it day to day within a stage? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Controlling a stage. The project manager controls the stage.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements are C O R R E C T? (one) Managing product delivery links the project manager and the team manager. (two) Managing a stage boundary happens at the end of the final stage. (three) Closing a project confirms acceptance of the project product. (four) Managing a stage boundary is carried out by the team manager. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and three. Statements one and three are correct.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. Managing a blank enables the board to approve the next stage plan. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Stage boundary. That is the stage boundary process.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which process produces the end project report? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Closing a project. Closing a project produces the end project report.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team manager receives a work package and returns the completed product. Which process is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Managing product delivery. That is managing product delivery.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. The board decides to stop a project early. Which process is used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Closing a project (premature close). A premature close uses closing a project.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of controlling a stage? Answer: Assign and monitor work, handle issues, report progress and keep the stage within tolerance. Question two. Who works in managing product delivery? Answer: The team manager(s), linked with the project manager. Question three. When does managing a stage boundary occur? Answer: Near the end of each stage except the last.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does closing a project confirm? Answer: Acceptance of the project product. Question five. Name two outputs of managing a stage boundary. Answer: The end stage report and the next stage plan. Question six. What is a premature close? Answer: Closing the project early because the board decides to stop it.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Process: Purpose in a phrase. Controlling a stage: assign, monitor, report, correct. Managing product delivery: accept, execute, deliver work packages. Managing a stage boundary: review stage, plan next, confirm business case. Closing a project: confirm acceptance, hand over, lessons.
